newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Schroeder stakes future on state poll.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Schroeder stakes future on state poll.

text.p: Gerhard Schroeder, the politician many Germans would like to see as chancellor, said on Friday his chances of challenging Helmut Kohl for the top job depended on regional elections early next year.
Schroeder, a senior member of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said his fate was linked to March 1998 state assembly elections in Lower Saxony, where he is premier.

Schroeder said if his party lost more than two percent of its support in Lower Saxony he would be too badly damaged to stand as the SPD's candidate for chancellor in general elections scheduled for September next year.

"I'm making the criteria for success apply to me," Schroeder told German news television station n-tv. "You won't need to speculate (on whether I shall stand) if there's a loss of more than two percent"

Polls regularly show Schroeder well ahead of Kohl as Germans' favourite for chancellor but even if he does well in Lower Saxony, there is still no guarantee his party will choose him to take on the veteran Christian Democrat.
SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine has not ruled out running against Kohl himself, although the chancellor beat him soundly in 1990 general elections.
Schroeder led the Lower Saxony SPD to 44.3 percent of the vote in the last state elections there in 1994.
